result:
I’d make high-quality education—focused not just on facts but on critical thinking, empathy, media literacy, and practical life skills—universally accessible from childhood through adulthood.

That one change wouldn’t solve everything by itself, but it would give more people the tools to recognize manipulation, make better collective decisions, understand each other across differences, and build solutions to problems like poverty, injustice, and environmental harm. In a sense, it’s a leverage point: better education doesn’t guarantee a better world, but it makes one far more possible.
